$comment: design §7.4's DECIDABLE restrictions, as data. The semantic bars of the same section — leftward reformulation, retirement reasons, facts kept verbatim — are not here: they reach S7 and S7b as the one canonical text in `packets/placement_contract.md` and are judged by S7b. Together this table and that packet are the single authority for §7.4, and WP-22 generates the runbook's contract section from them (never hand-written). `runlib/placement.py` reads this file; `placement.fidelity_problems` holds the rule ids plus the packet's bars against the copied and cited §7.4 list.

destinations.$comment: the layers as destinations, in §7.4's order of 'cheapest that still fires on time'. The order is data because the rule is an order, and a reader that re-sorted it would be a second authority.
destinations.global_file: the always-loaded global file, which §7.4's revision leaves open to deletions and merges only

consumers.$comment: consumer escalation (§7.4): who executes when the learning is needed. A consumer that reads only code cannot be reached by an instruction, whatever layer it is placed in.

rules.design: a guide proposed where fewer than five promoted items share a situation no guide covers
an instruction aimed at a consumer that reads only code (a script, a hermetic dispatch)
a blocking gate proposed for a semantic criterion
an addition to the global file
rules.$comment: §7.4's destination rule, beside §7.3's operation rule in tables/structural_rules.json: one refuses the always-loaded file as the HOME of a new learning, the other refuses an operation on it that is not a delete or a merge. Both can hold of one proposal, and each says which it was.

rules.design: a C principle routed anywhere but the router trigger of the guide whose situation it names or session-level injection
a hook that blocks or judges
rules.$comment: the hook charter of §7.4: pattern-matched injection of canonical text, no blocking and no semantic judging.

$comment_inputs: Each rule names the inputs it READS and the scope in which it reads them. `placement.py` refuses a proposal that is in a rule's scope and does not carry one of that rule's inputs (PLACEMENT_INPUT_ABSENT) instead of letting the rule pass over a field nobody filled. The reason is measured: the flat proposal S7 built carried none of these, so five of the six rules passed vacuously on every proposal while their own suite - which calls them with hand-built dicts - stayed green. A rule whose input never arrives is not a rule.
